title: UniformDirectImageBoundCore
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated with $S$ quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme]. There exists an integer $N>0$ such that for every $E\in D_{QCoh}(O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] with $H^m(E)=0$ for $m>0$, one has $H^m(Rf_*E)=0$ for $m\ge N$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image].

proof.text: Choose the uniform integer $n_0$ supplied by clause 2 of [lem-pc-finite-support-hi] for $f$, and put $N=\max(1,n_0)$. The same bound holds for every base change of $f$, in particular for $f_U:f^{-1}U\to U$ over each affine open $U\subseteq S$. For every quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ on $f^{-1}U$, all $R^pf_{U,*}\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent and vanish for $p\ge N$.

source.place: Tag 08D5 proof, choice of N from Tag 01XJ; Tag 01XJ clauses 1-3

proof.text: For an affine open $U\subseteq S$, each $R^pf_{U,*}\mathcal F$ in Step 1 is quasi-coherent, so its higher cohomology on $U$ vanishes by [lem-pc-affine-vanishing]. Clause 2 of [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections] then identifies $H^p(f^{-1}U,\mathcal F)$ with $\Gamma(U,R^pf_{U,*}\mathcal F)$ for every $p\ge0$. The latter group is zero for $p\ge N$ by Step 1. Thus the right derived functors of $\Gamma(f^{-1}U,-)$ vanish in degrees $p\ge N$ on every quasi-coherent module. By [pqf-def-cohomology], these cohomology groups are the right derived functors of global sections. The functor $\Gamma(f^{-1}U,-)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_{f^{-1}U},-)$ commutes with countable products because a morphism into a product is uniquely a family of morphisms into its factors; this is a direct check from the product universal property.

source.place: Tag 08D5 proof of part (2), Tag 01XK and Tag 08D4 hypotheses

proof.text: Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ have $H^i(E)=0$ for $i>0$. Its restriction to $f^{-1}U$ has the same property and quasi-coherent cohomology. Apply [lem-pc-unbounded-derived-functor-cohomological-bound] to $F=\Gamma(f^{-1}U,-)$ with $b=0$ and the $N$ of Step 1; Step 2 checks its product and acyclicity hypotheses. Hence $H^i(R\Gamma(f^{-1}U,E))=0$ for $i>N-1$, equivalently $i\ge N$. By [lem-pc-derived-sections-pushforward-comparison] this equals $H^i(R\Gamma(U,Rf_*E))$. These vanishings on every affine $U$ imply $H^i(Rf_*E)=0$: take a K-injective representative $I$ of $Rf_*E$; its cohomology sheaf is the sheafification of $U\mapsto H^i(\Gamma(U,I))$, and derived sections compute those groups. Thus the affine-basis sections of that presheaf vanish, and so does its sheafification. For the restriction identification, choose a K-injective representative of $E$; [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open] keeps its restriction K-injective, and the equality of direct-image sections on $U$ follows termwise from $(f_*I)|_U=(f_U)_*(I|_{f^{-1}U})$. Hence $Rf_*E|_U\simeq R(f_U)_*(E|_{f^{-1}U})$.

source.place: Tag 08D5 proof of part (2), application of Tag 08D4 to Gamma(f^{-1}U,-) and displayed derived-sections identity

lean.statement:
theorem uniform_bound_core
    {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace))]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [CompactSpace S] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, 0 < N ∧
      ∀ E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory X,
        (∀ m : ℤ, 0 < m → IsZero
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) m).obj E.obj)) →
        ∀ m : ℤ, N ≤ m → IsZero ((schemeHigherDirectImage f m).obj E.obj)
